In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general Nakagamim fading channels, orthogonal STBCs provide a diversity order equal to the number of transmit antennas, and that, for the high SNR regime, the optimal power allocation strategy is to assign the transmit antennas with identical Nakagami-m parameters the same power and, otherwise, to assign more power to the antennas with higher Nakagami-m parameter values.

the optimal power allocation strategy for the high SNR regime is to allocate the transmit power equally among the transmit antennas, while the optimal strategy for the low SNR is to allocate all transmit power to the antenna with the best channel quality.
, in general, the optimal power allocation strategy is not the same for all the Nakagami-m cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general Nakagamim fading channels with not necessarily identical fading parameter values, orthogonal STBC in conjunction with optimal power allocation can achieve full diversity and coding gain equal to that in the case of identical fading parameter values.

, in the high SNR regime, optimal power allocation improves the BER performance of M-ary QAM by a factor of 2m+1, where m is the Nakagami-m parameter, and that the optimal power allocation is achieved when the power is allocated to the subchannels in proportion to the square root of their average power gains.

we have derived the exact and asymptotic expressions for the BER of M-ary QAM for orthogonal STBC in general Nakagamim fading channels, and we have derived the optimal power allocation schemes for this system in both high and low SNRs, assuming that statistical knowledge of the fading parameters is available at the transmit side.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal power allocation strategy is not necessarily uniform and that it can be quite sensitive to the value of the fading parameters.

, for a fixed number of transmit antennas, the optimal power allocation strategy for the high SNR regime is the same for any value of the fading parameters, while for the low SNR case, the optimal power allocations depend on the fading parameters and the number of receive antennas.
, in general Nakagamim fading channels, optimal power allocation can significantly enhance the BER performance of MIMO systems employing orthogonal STBC.
